text:
maya: FYI we saw a noisy-tenant incident in canary this morning where one customer burned credits and filled all burst slots. Neighbor tenants saw p95 spike ~40s. Not full outage but noisy.

katie: Can you paste the admission ledger? Curious whether admits were serialized or parallelized.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: admit_log window_start=1765999940 window_end=1766000000 admits=128 drops=12 preempts=6

liu: Quick summary from traces: tenant A consumed ~85% of its burst bucket in 22s. Admission layer continued admitting until pool soft-cap hit, then eviction TTL stalled.

sahil: Two failure modes we should address: (A) aggressive single-tenant burn without graceful throttle, (B) slow drain that holds resources longer than necessary.

alex: For (A) proposal: per-tenant sliding-bucket + progressive cool-down. When burn_rate > threshold, reduce admit window by factor f and return an HTTP 429 with Retry-After hint that maps to ticket lifetime. Also emit metric admit_cooldown{tenant}.

maya: Example policy I ran in staging (different knobs):
```
admit_filter:
  tenant_throttle:
    enabled: true
    burn_threshold_tokens_per_sec: 5
    cool_down_secs_base: 30
    cool_down_backoff: 1.5
    max_cool_down: 300
```

katie: We need to be careful with 429 semantics for long-polling SDKs. Some SDKs retry aggressively. We should provide a header X-Redwood-Backoff with machine-readable reason & suggested retry window.

liu: Also add tier-aware exemptions: enterprise tenants with active SLA can be given a small reserve or slower backoff. We need to wire tenant_tier into the admit decision.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: reserve_check tenant=tenant-A tier=standard reserve=0.5 1766000085

alex: For (B) drain improvements I sketched: fast-drain mode that switches pods to a force-evict path if they've been draining > drain_max_secs or if global headroom < headroom_threshold. Force-evict will: close idle conns after N sec, attempt to reschedule inflight to fallback pool (if compatible), and persist warm-kv reference so fallback can warm quickly.

maya: Important: the fallback handshake must not leak secrets. If we persist any auth metadata for warm-up, use short-lived tokens and KMS-wrapped blobs. Tagging @security for review.

katie: Also tracking cost impact: fallback warmups increase tokens and small models may see higher unit cost. Add a cost_estimate event to the rollout metrics.

liu: Suggested rollout plan:
- step 0: safe read-only config + metrics (canary)
- step 1: enable tenant_throttle=true in canary for 48h, monitor deferred_admits and tenant_slo_impact
- step 2: enable drain fast-evict only for preemption in canary 24h
- step 3: gradual ramp to regional Dedicated pools with kill-switch and SLA overrides

alex: I'll take the drain fast-evict patch. Plan to add unit tests for finalizer cleanup.

maya: I'll draft the RFC for "tenant-throttle + fast-evict drain". Will include config schema, metrics to export, and expected SLO deltas for neighbors.

sahil: I'll build the E2E harness that simulates high-burn tenant and asserts neighbor p95 and error surfaces. Also will add a test for SDK behavior on 429 + X-Redwood-Backoff header.

autoscaler-bot: alert: create("noisy-tenant-cooldown-applied") created_by=maya for canary test 1766000150

katie: Small ask: expose per-tenant recent_burn_rate in internal dashboard + a histogram of cooldown durations. That made debugging earlier incidents much faster.

liu: Another minor: when moving inflight requests to fallback, ensure request attribution / billing tags are preserved. We need ledger continuity.

maya: Good point. We'll include a billing-tag passthrough in the handshake proto. Security, confirm acceptable fields.

autoscaler-bot: fallback_route_attempt tenant=tenant-A from_pool=burst to_pool=redwood-small status=warmup_started 1766000175

alex: Let's keep knobs minimal initially: default cool_down_secs_base=30, backoff=1.5, enabled=false by default. Document kill-switch and emergency revert playbook in the RFC.

maya: Agreed. I'll add rollbacks and required observability thresholds (p95 of neighbors, deferred_admit_rate, tenant_error_rate).

sahil: Great. I'll queue the E2E for tomorrow and tag QA. Thanks all. :rocket:

maya: RFC link (WIP): https://r.redwood/ops/rfcs/tenant-throttle-drain-evict

katie: tagging @eng-sre and @security for reviews.

maya: closing thread; will follow up in RFC and PRs.
